title: Warroom stakeholder lanecards and status cadence (draft)
summary: Draft set of lane-card messages, status page templates, customer-facing blurbs, and an internal war-room checklist with a proposed cadence for live updates. Designed to reduce time-to-first-message and make stakeholder messaging consistent across Sev1/Sev2 incidents.
body:
BACKGROUND
Purpose: provide one-page lane-cards for common stakeholders (executive, sales, customer success, legal), a set of short status-page templates (initial/update/resolved), sample customer email/snippets, and an internal rapid-check checklist for the first 60 minutes of a Sev1/Sev2.

HOW TO USE
- Owner (incident commander) reads lane-card corresponding to the incident severity and audience.
- Use the status page templates verbatim when possible; shorten if constrained by legal/CS review time.
- Follow the internal checklist during the first 60 minutes. The cadence table indicates suggested update frequency.

STATUS PAGE TEMPLATES
1) Initial (aim to post within 10–20 minutes):
Title: Degraded service for Redwood API — investigating
Body: We are aware of increased errors and/or elevated latency affecting {product_area} for some customers. Our teams are investigating. Impact: {brief impact statement — e.g., "API errors for <10% of requests"}. Scope: {regions/tenants affected if known}. ETA: We are working on a fix and will post an update by {ETA_window}. Status: Investigating.
Meta: severity: {S1|S2}, started_at: {UTC timestamp}.

2) Update (every 30 min for S1, every 60 min for S2 or per cadence):
Title: Update: Redwood API incident — progress update
Body: Summary of what we learned, what we are doing next, and any customer mitigations/workarounds. Example: "We identified a regression in the request router causing cache thrashing; rolling a rollback to the previous router build. Customers may see brief errors during the rollback window."
Include: progress (%), next ETA, customer action required (if any).

3) Resolved
Title: Resolved: Redwood API incident affecting {product_area}
Body: The issue has been resolved at {timestamp UTC}. Root cause (short): {one-line root cause}. Customer impact: {summary — e.g., duration, percent of requests affected}. Postmortem link: {link when available}. Apology line and contact: "We apologize for the disruption. If you need assistance, contact support@redwood.ai or your account team."

CUSTOMER-FACING SNIPPETS (channel-specific)
- In-app banner (short): "We experienced an outage affecting {product_area}. Full service restored at {time} — more details on status.redwood.ai."
- Email subject (urgent): "Service outage affecting Redwood API — {start_time} UTC"
- Email body (concise): "Hi {CustomerName}, we're writing to let you know we experienced an outage impacting {product_feature}. Services were degraded between {start} and {end}. We have restored service and are investigating root cause. We will follow up with a postmortem." Include dedicated CS contact and link to status page.
- Slack customer-facing: "[STATUS] Resolved — Redwood API errors impacting text-generation from {start} to {end}. More: {status_link}."

STAKEHOLDER LANE-CARDS (quick scripts)
- Executive (C-suite) — 1–2 lines, no tech detail: "We had a service incident affecting parts of the Redwood API starting at {time}. Impact was limited to {scope}. Engineers have restored service; we're investigating root cause and will follow up with a postmortem. No customer data exposure identified." (When customer data exposure: escalate to Legal immediately and modify wording to reflect ongoing investigation.)

- Sales — 2–3 lines, indicate customer impact and next steps: "Heads-up: Some customers may have seen elevated errors between {start}–{end}. Affected customers should contact support; we'll provide notes for account outreach and a postmortem." Attach suggested customer list if known.

- Customer Success — full context + CS script: provide timeline, workaround, recommended outreach cadence (email + proactive account outreach for top 20 customers), and link to composeable email template above.

- Legal & Compliance — include potential data exposure flag, timeline, and any regulators to notify. Keep language factual and avoid speculation.

INTERNAL WAR-ROOM CHECKLIST (first 60 minutes)
- 0–5 min: Incident declared. IC assigned, comm lead assigned, Scribe assigned, triage channel created (#warroom-<incident-id>). Post initial status page (use template).
- 5–15 min: Confirm scope and impact metrics (error rate, latency, affected regions/tenants). Capture initial artifacts: logs, tracing links, deploys in last 24h. Identify potential rollback/mitigation.
- 15–30 min: Implement immediate mitigation (traffic reroute/rollback/scale) if safe. Notify customer-facing teams of expected behavior. Prepare next status update.
- 30–60 min: Measure mitigation effectiveness. If not improving, escalate to engineering manager/Sr Eng for hypercare. Draft customer email if impact persists >30–60 min.
- Roles reminder: IC = incident commander (coordinates), Tech lead = root-cause owner, SRE = runs mitigation steps, Comms = posts status messages and crafts customer emails, CS/Acct = outreach to named customers.

CADENCE & CHANNELS
- Public status page: initial within 10–20 min, updates every 30 min for Sev1, every 60–90 min for Sev2 until resolved.
- Customer emails: Send if incident >30 min or any named customer impacted. Use CS to tailor messages for top accounts.
- Internal updates: Slack war-room every 15 min for first hour, then every 30 min while active. IC decides to increase cadence.
- Executive brief: ping execs at 30 min and again at resolution for Sev1. Provide one-line update via email/Slack.

ESCALATION TRIGGERS
- No measurable improvement within 30 min after mitigation attempt
- Errors affecting >10% of production requests
- Named customer(s) report severe business impact (revenue/SLAs)
- Potential data integrity/exposure

POST-RESOLUTION NEXT STEPS (short)
- Postmortem owner assigned within 24 hours.
- Timeline & RCA draft due within 72 hours, final within 7 days for Sev1.
- CS/Acct: outreach log (who we contacted and when) stored in the incident doc.

QUICK REFERENCE: SUBJECT LINES & SHORT MESSAGES
- Initial status page: "Investigating: Service degradation for Redwood API"
- Exec Slack: "FYI: Incident impacting API — investigating; will update in 30m"
- Customer email subj: "Redwood API incident — {start_date}"
- Resolved banner: "Service restored — Redwood API"

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODO (work-in-progress)
- Should we standardize a 10-minute 'notify all execs' rule for Sev1? pros/cons.
- Draft a short webhook for product usage dashboards to auto-attach current QPS to status page updates.
- Validate legal-approved wording for data-exposure language.

ATTACHMENTS & REFERENCES
- Templates: copy/paste blocks above for quick insertion
- Links: Add postmortem stub in Confluence and link here after incident closes.

NOTES TO SELF
- Keep messages short and human; customers prefer honesty and actionable next steps.
- Avoid deep technical detail in public messages; use CS to provide more specifics privately to affected customers.

END
